newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude under pressure as buyers take stock.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude under pressure as buyers take stock.

text.p: Brent crude values were notionally higher in afternoon business and paper spreads held steady but the physical market was enfeebled by the depressed value of Dated Brent, brokers said.

Jan 15-day Brent traded at $23.35 a barrel in the London afternoon, in line with screen levels. The Dec/Jan spread helds its 37-cent backwardation, while the prompt to Dated spread remained in a 35-40 cent contango.

CFD business was active with next week's dates done at Jan +10 cents, some eight cents below Thursday levels. A roll of Nov 12-15 into Nov 18-22 was done at -2 cents and a Nov 18-Dec 13 CFD traded twice at Jan +9 cents.
One trader said the fact that the CFD backwardation curve had come in pointed to perceptions of a weaker market.

The physical market was also depressed with an overhang of unsold barrels prompting sellers to accept lower numbers. Holders of prompt North Sea barrels were struggling to get a premium of a few cents over Dated Brent.
A Nov 7-9 Statfjord was sold at Dated Brent +5 cents a day after a distressed Forties cargo went for December Brent +2 cents.

"People are covered for now and you will only see buyers coming in for additional supplies. It is a question of space, because people bought so much when they were going flat out," a trader for an oil company said.
Dated Brent talk was thin after a November 8-10 loader fetched Dec Brent -40 cents on Thursay. The holder of a Nov 15-17 cargo was considering offering at Jan Brent +15/+10 cents, traders said.

The situation was much the same in the West African market. One trader heard a Nov 20 Brass/Forcados combi cargo traded at Dated Brent +40 cents for the Brass element and +52 cents for Forcados into the Med.
